1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: v3 after 17 independent review rounds; approved by the owner 2026-11-09 · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes or links the official page (a few rows cite vendor blogs, bulletins or example files instead, e.g. R2.4.1b, R6.3.5, R5.5.4). |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	This is a design without access to Papaya's systems; nothing was run against them. The files in
21	[`examples/`](../examples/README.md) were checked locally (✅, commands and output there), and
22	"examples finding n" / "E*n*" point to that file.
23	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
24	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
25	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
26	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
27	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 1. The decision in one page
32	
33	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
34	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
35	
36	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
37	
38	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
39	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
40	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
41	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, ⚠️ R2.9 #3) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
42	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
43	
44	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
45	|---|---|
46	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
47	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
48	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
49	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
50	
51	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
52	
53	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
54	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
55	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
56	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
57	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
58	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an owner of the stack approves the prod preview [design].
59	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
60	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
61	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
62	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
63	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
64	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
65	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
66	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** code-owner review means an approver must own the file,
67	  at L2 as at L3. So that one on-call primary can approve any deployable path at 2 a.m., the on-call approver
68	  group co-owns every deployable path (owner decision OD9, layer 3). The cost: GitHub accepts an
69	  approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve another
70	  domain's PR. Domain review on normal days becomes a process rule with a monthly check, not a
71	  technical control. Because on-call approvers only
72	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
73	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
74	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
75	  approver, like L2, but the path is owned by the L3 owner team (or by the stack's owners for L3
76	  content in domain files, OD8), and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
77	  the prod preview (OD2, OD8, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
78	  for speed.
79	- **k0s and Firebase are weaker:** no prod preview or risk stop, no CloudTrail for k0s changes
80	  (so S3 reconciliation does not cover them), and no break-glass when Actions is down (G1, G2).
81	- **New dependencies on two GitHub Apps** (required check, CI agent): if the required-check app is
82	  down, every merge to `main` is blocked, incident PRs included; that counts as "pipeline
83	  unavailable" for JIT. Their keys and hosting are open (G19).
84	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
85	  business associate, as the brief implies.
86	
87	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
88	
89	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
90	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
91	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
92	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
93	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.

109	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
110	
111	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
112	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
113	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
114	
115	**On Papaya's stack**
116	
117	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
118	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
119	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
120	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
121	  holds.
122	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
123	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
124	    accepted as a process control, D2);
125	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
126	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
127	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
128	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
129	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
130	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
131	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
132	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
133	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
134	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
135	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
136	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Some "metadata" reads return configuration or
137	    secrets, so `Resource: "*"` only for a reviewed action list (examples E6, findings 11, 12). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
138	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
139	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
140	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
141	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
142	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
143	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
144	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
145	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
146	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
147	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
148	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
149	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
150	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
151	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
152	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
153	    JIT roles. The Serverless prod deploy role is a separate role and is not exempt: it only passes
154	    the `deploymentRole` (examples finding 13). This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
155	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
156	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:UserId` (📖 R2.4.4); deny changes to any trail
157	    in prod accounts, since member accounts cannot touch the organization trail anyway (📖 R2.6.2;
158	    examples findings 10, 15);
159	  - exempt role names are protected: only the Pulumi prod deploy role may change such roles (OD19;
160	    until OD20, "only an approved prod Pulumi deploy"; examples findings 14, 16).
161	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
162	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path, held by the L3 owner team only, not co-owned by the on-call group; OD13).

171	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP

173	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).

177	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write and keep a free non-prod loop. Prod reads stay
178	fast for metrics and metadata, but shrink during the transition: because the engineer's access is the
179	agent's access, from phase 1 the engineer too loses raw logs and configuration of services not yet
180	redacted or moved to runtime secrets. Configuration values come from the IaC code instead (layer 1
181	above); raw logs that may hold customer data need an L3-data grant. The data owner is not on the
182	on-call schedule, so at night the grant is approved by the on-call approver alone and the data owner
183	reviews it the next working day [design]; the wait still counts against S7. This is
184	the largest cost of the first months. Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

191	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
192	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).

276	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
277	
278	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
279	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
280	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and

280	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
281	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
282	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
283	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
284	second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
285	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
286	approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
287	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
288	approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
289	OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
290	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
291	
292	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
293	|---|---|---|---|---|
294	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
295	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
296	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
297	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
298	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
299	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |
300	
301	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
302	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
303	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
304	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
305	L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
306	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by

308	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
309	the domain team that edits it most.

312	
313	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
314	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,

A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5), set by a dedicated GitHub App that reacts to review events and is the pinned source [design; hosting, key storage and whether its key counts against S2 are not researched, ⚠️ G19], adds what

391	
392	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
393	unavailable).
394	
395	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
396	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
397	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
398	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
399	3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
400	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
401	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
402	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
403	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.

448	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
449	
450	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
451	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
452	checks as human code (S10).
453	
454	**On Papaya's stack**
455	
456	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
457	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
458	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
459	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
460	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
461	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
462	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
463	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
464	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
465	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
466	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
467	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
468	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
469	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
470	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
471	    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
472	    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can likely target the runner's label (⚠️ G15).
473	    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
474	    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
475	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
476	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
477	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
478	  - optionally a separate environment (e.g. `production-k0s`), limited to `main` and referenced
479	    only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read these secrets
480	    [design].
481	
482	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
483	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
484	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
485	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
486	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
487	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
488	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
489	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
490	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (availability on Team ⚠️); the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
491	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
492	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
493	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, `.devcontainer/` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5, R6.3.11), plus
494	  `.npmrc` (registry redirection) [design], the policy packs, the SCP code, the
495	  catalogue file and the risk-stop classifier `tools/risk-stop/` (OD14: the deploy runs it from the
496	  merged commit, so a domain-approved PR could otherwise switch it off). This is the canonical L3 path list that layer 3 refers to. Not on it:
497	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`, owned by the stack's owners and the on-call group (OD8, OD9). The private plugin
498	  marketplace is a separate repo and needs its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS [design]. CI validates the file, because
499	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7). A fail-safe default line (`*` → L3 owner team and
500	  on-call group) keeps new stacks and root files from being unowned, since an unowned file accepts
501	  an approval from any writer (examples finding 7) [design].
502	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
503	  📖 R3.5.4).
504	- **Agent review:** an independent agent (not the one that made the change) may post an automated
505	  review as an extra check; it never counts as an approval (GĐ-11).
506	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
507	  requests (📖 R1.7.8), whose own credentials are listed in the S2 inventory (⚠️ G19); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
508	  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
509	  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
510	  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
511	  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),

513	- **App-opened PRs:** a required check set by a dedicated GitHub App, pinned as its source (layer 3), confirms at least one approval by a
514	  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
515	  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).

518	  (📖 R4.2.2). For Serverless stacks, Access Analyzer would check the IAM policies in the
519	  CloudFormation template that `serverless package` produces, against the deployed ones (⚠️ not

526	**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git, the secrets inventory and exception register (S2), audit-log events for secrets and Actions settings, and check results per PR; full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).

533	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
534	
535	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
536	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
537	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
538	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
539	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
540	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
541	
542	**On Papaya's stack**
543	
544	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
545	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
546	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
547	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
548	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
549	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
550	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
551	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
552	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
553	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
554	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. At night the data owner is not on call: the
555	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day. This
556	  applies to non-PHI and PHI alike; for PHI the reader is still a human without an agent. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
557	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
558	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
559	    redacted summary. This
560	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
561	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
562	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
563	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
564	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
565	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
566	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
567	  1.11.4 L6).
568	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
569	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
570	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
571	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
572	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
573	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
574	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
575	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
576	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
577	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
578	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
579	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
580	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
581	  not part of the free loop.
582	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
583	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
584	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
585	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
586	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
587	
588	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data, real-data requests with the data-read role's CloudTrail events, and non-prod scan results; full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
589	
590	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
591	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
592	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
593	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).
594	
595	---
596	
597	## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass
598	
599	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
600	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
601	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
602	
603	**On Papaya's stack**
604	
605	- **Audit stores:**
606	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
607	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
608	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
609	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
610	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
611	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
612	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
613	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
614	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
615	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
616	    with an expected copy (G8);
617	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
618	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
619	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
620	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
621	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
622	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
623	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
624	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
625	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
626	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
627	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
628	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
629	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
630	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
631	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
632	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
633	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
634	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
635	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
636	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
637	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
638	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
639	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
640	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
641	
642	  | Step | Rule |
643	  |---|---|
644	  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
645	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
646	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
647	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
648	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
649	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
650	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
651	
652	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
653	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
654	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
655	
656	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
657	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
658	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
659	  this draft). On a breach,
660	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
661	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
662	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
663	  (D2, ⚠️).
664	
665	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail, the exported GitHub audit log, change records and monthly reconciliation (S3, S8), JIT records, drift tickets and incident approval waits (S7); full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
666	
667	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
668	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
669	incidents, plus detection.
670	
671	---
672	
673	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
674	
675	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
676	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
677	attacks.
678	
679	**On Papaya's stack**
680	
681	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
682	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
683	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
684	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
685	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
686	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
687	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
688	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
689	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
690	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
691	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed): [`03-rollout-plan.md`](03-rollout-plan.md), moved
692	  there unchanged. Order (framing Q8): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow standing prod
693	  access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2). Phase 1 (0–30 days)
694	  makes the PR the only prod write path, with six hard prerequisites before standing prod write is
695	  removed; phase 2 (30–60) adds SCPs, the rest of the managed baseline and automated
696	  reconciliation; phase 3 (60–90) tests and reviews. The phase-1 load on 1–2 DevSecOps people is the
697	  main rollout risk [design; effort not estimated ⚠️].
698	
699	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
700	- **Standards mapping:** ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (IDs recalled, ⚠️ R5.1), HIPAA Security Rule
701	  (📖 R5.2) and Vietnam law (📖 R5.4) are mapped per control area in the
702	  [compliance register](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference), with every caveat. "A named human approves"
703	  is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
704	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
705	
706	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files, monthly metrics, 90-day review minutes, the exception register and planted-injection reports; standards: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference).
707	
708	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system
709	with owners and review dates.
710	
711	---
712	
713	## Gaps (not covered, or only as an open item, in `work/02-research.md`)
714	
715	| # | Gap | Layers |
716	|---|---|---|
717	| G1 | k0s: authentication, RBAC, audit logging, kubeconfig issuance (GĐ-4); break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 3, 6, 7 |
718	| G2 | Firebase Hosting deploy from CI without a stored token; break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 5, 7 |
719	| G3 | Human and agent access to GCP (roles, data access) | 1, 6 |
720	| G4 | Secret scanning, dependency check, SAST, non-prod data scanning on the Team plan | 5, 6 |
721	| G5 | Paging and alert routing; approving a PR from a phone | 7 |
722	| G6 | SSM Automation `aws:approve` (read in `work/03-options.md` §2, not in 02-research) | 7 |
723	| G7 | GitHub Actions log and artifact retention, and export | 3, 7 |
724	| G8 | Rulesets and environment settings through the API | 7, 8 |
725	| G9 | How Linear and Slack MCP servers authenticate | 4, 6 |
726	| G10 | OIDC subject customisation (`job_workflow_ref`) on GitHub Team | 1 |
727	| G11 | Closing provider/login bypasses on laptops without MDM | 2 |
728	| G12 | `pulumi up` flag reference for the prod allowlist | 3 |
729	| G13 | IAM actions for every data-plane read (S3, SQS, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, RDS, ECS Exec, Lambda invoke) | 1, 6 |
730	| G14 | Which state writes a Pulumi refresh preview needs on a DIY S3 backend | 3, 7 |
731	| G15 | Restricting a self-hosted runner to one workflow in a monorepo; just-in-time runners | 5 |
732	| G16 | Managing GitHub team membership as code; audit event for a membership change | 3, 7 |
733	| G17 | Who forms the L3 owner team and how many people (GĐ-1: never a single reviewer) | 3, 8 |
734	| G18 | Reading the live values of server-managed settings (API or local cache) to compare with git | 2, 8 |

736	| G20 | Emergency revocation at night: who can apply the revocation Deny SCP (management account) within minutes; `aws:TokenIssueTime` kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3) | 1, 7 |
737	
738	Open checks from `work/03-options.md` §8 remain open.
739	
740	## Owner decisions (2026-11-09)
741	
742	The owner answered the open questions of draft v3. English rendering; the original Vietnamese
743	answers are recorded in `work/session-log.md`.
744	
745	| # | Question | Decision |
746	|---|---|---|
747	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |
748	| OD2 | L3: must one approver be from the platform team? | Not necessarily; one approval procedure is agreed for all engineers, and the on-call engineer is enough. Clarified in follow-ups: every change involves two people, one who makes it and one who approves; the on-call backup only replaces an unavailable primary. Asked whether L3 should need more approvers than L2, the owner chose "L3 = 1 approver at all times"; in the agent's framing of that option, the approver must own the path. |
749	| OD3 | `CLAUDE.md` changes: L2 or L3? | L3, because the workflow must be consistent across the whole team. |
750	| OD4 | Move the rest of the managed baseline and the SSM check to phase 2? | Yes. |
751	| OD5 | "An agent does not approve PRs" only a process rule? | It is a rule: the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent. |
752	| OD6 | Scope of OD1: CI deploy credentials only, or also runtime scaling credentials? | CI deploy credentials (k0s kubeconfig/token, Firebase token in GitHub secrets) only, until it is checked whether k0s and Firebase can use OIDC. |
753	| OD7 | (a) If the on-call engineer writes an L3 fix, who approves? (b) Keep the read-only allowlist in phase 1? | (a) "While on call, never change the process"; clarified: on-call engineers only approve, and fixes are written by another engineer (the incident responder), so the approver is never the author. (b) Yes, as proposed. |
754	| OD8 | IAM/network/stateful changes inside a domain file: who approves the risk stop? | The stack's owners (may be the first approver); always two people. The L3 owner team keeps only the real L3 paths; Access Analyzer and policy packs compensate. |
755	| OD9 | How can one on-call primary approve any path at night? | The on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path; one primary + one backup. Normal-day domain review is a process rule with a monthly check. |
756	| OD10 | A PR touching files of several domain teams: split, or one approval? | One approval is enough (two-person rule kept); domain review on such PRs is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. |
757	| OD11 | Risk stop when the first approver is unavailable: may another owner of the stack approve? | Yes; it makes three people and is recorded as a deviation. |
758	| OD12 | `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`: `true` or `false`? | Keep `true` (fewer prompts, relies on the sandbox, which arrives in phase 2). |
759	| OD13 | Confirm three agent readings: (1) OD8, who opens and approves the risk-stop approval PR; (2) OD9, scope of the on-call group; (3) L3-JIT, does the on-call approver count as service owner? | Confirmed: (1) the original author opens it and the first approver approves it; (2) the on-call group does not co-own process-defining paths or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves; (3) yes. |
760	| OD14 | Add the risk-stop classifier (`tools/risk-stop/`) to the canonical L3 path list? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes: it is a control, so only the L3 owner team may change it. |
761	| OD15 | Scope of the risk stop: risky diffs nobody looked at, or also malicious approved code? | Keep the current scope and state its limits; a separate prod preview role and a job split go to the phase-2 roadmap. |
762	| OD16 | Squash-only merges to `main` (needed so a PR cannot carry its own risk-stop approval)? | Yes; the cost is that PR-internal commit history is not kept on `main`. |
763	| OD17 | Deploy only the current tip of `main`, so re-running an old run cannot roll prod back? | Yes; added to the layer-3 "merge approval = deploy approval" conditions. |
764	| OD18 | An approval merged before a deploy stops, matched by a later change outside the stack's directory, is still accepted | Accepted as a stated limit; the approval-gate app (G19) is to close it by checking the stopped run's hash. |
765	| OD19 | Protect the names of SCP-exempt roles (`app-claims-*`, `cfn-deployment-*`, `github-prod-deploy-*`) so that only the IAM stack's deploy role can create or change them? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes. Confirmed reading: "only the IAM stack" holds once OD20 gives the IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod Pulumi deploy". |
766	| OD20 | Code in the deploy job (install scripts, Pulumi program, Serverless plugins) can request the job's OIDC token for either prod deploy role: fix now or roadmap? | Roadmap phase 2, together with OD15: a build job without `id-token`, and per-role environments (different OIDC subjects) or `job_workflow_ref`. Until then it is a stated limit. |
767	| OD21 | Phase 1 lets built-in read-only commands (`cat`, `head` …) read `~/.aws` without a prompt, and allow rules skip the auto-mode classifier: add keys to the phase-1 subset? | Yes: add a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` (examples finding 19). |

    16	**CO** Compliance · **EL** engineering leads · **EM** engineering management.

    19	standing prod access, (3) the MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list comes before or with (2).

## Evidence for one prod change (S8)

**Target** (framing §5): for a prod change picked at random, show who proposed, who approved, what
was approved, what was applied and when, in ≤ 30 minutes, without asking anyone. Not yet timed
(⚠️; first measured in rollout).

Start **backward**, from a prod write in CloudTrail: unlike starting from a PR, this also finds
unapproved writes, as the monthly reconciliation does (S3).

| Step | Question | Record | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What was applied, when? | Write event: `eventTime`, `eventName`, resource; session name `deploy-<run_id>-<attempt>` [design, E3] in `principalId` (📖 R2.5.3) | CloudTrail; digests prove integrity (📖 R2.6.4) |
| 2 | Which run? | Run ID → deploy run: stack, commit SHA, preview, risk-stop result | Actions log (⚠️ G7; export Ph 2) |
| 3 | What was approved? | SHA → squash-merged PR (OD16). Stale approvals are dismissed (📖 R3.2.3), so approval covers the final diff | GitHub PR |
| 4 | Who proposed? | PR author; for an app-opened PR, the person who triggered it, from the approval-gate check (G19) | GitHub PR |
| 5 | Who approved, before apply? | Review name and time; approver ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3, R3.3.1); approver owns the path (CODEOWNERS at that commit). Approval < merge < `eventTime` | GitHub PR; git |
| 6 | Was the gate on? | E1 copy; no `repository_ruleset.update` or `protected_branch.policy_override` in the window; G8 results | git; audit-log export |
| 7 | Did the risk stop fire? | `risk-summary`; `deploy-approvals/` PR with hash and stack-owner approval; second run shows the hash matched | artifact (⚠️ G7); git; PR |

From Ph 2 the change record (C-19) holds these links, so steps 2–7 are one lookup. In Ph 1 there is
no change record, export or reconciliation: the auditor follows links by hand, and old records may be
gone (audit log 180 days, 📖 R3.5.6; Actions ⚠️ G7). S8 is realistic only from Ph 2 (⚠️ inference).

**Serverless stacks:** CloudFormation makes the changes with the stack's `deploymentRole` (layer 3),
so those events may not carry the run's session name (⚠️ not researched). The link is the deploy
session's CloudFormation call plus the stack's events.

**Incident lane:** the same chain, plus the `incident` label and the on-call schedule showing the
approver was the primary on shift, or the backup while the primary was unavailable (O-7). The wait
(S7) runs from review request to approval. In Ph 1 the approver is called by phone, so paging time is
not recorded (G5).

**JIT fallback**, keyed by the JIT request ID ([layer 7](01-framework.md#layer-7--observability-audit-incident-response-and-break-glass)):
(1) proposed: command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel independent of GitHub (O-1);
(2) approved: on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; (3) granted: `CreateAccountAssignment`
and `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); (4) applied: CloudTrail writes of the
`InfraOperator-<service>` session, the human named by session name and directory lookup, not a
stable key (⚠️ R2.5.3); (5) reconciled: writes compared with the list, codify PR merged, drift
ticket until then. The approver approved a **command list**, not the applied change; a write outside
the list is found afterwards, not prevented.

## Known gaps for Compliance

**Approval before apply, met only partly:**

1. **JIT fallback**, accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2, [§1](01-framework.md#1-the-decision-in-one-page)).
   Window up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.9 #3); no night-time revocation (G20).
2. **Process-only rules**, checked by sampling or monthly reports: an agent never approves; its
   approval through the engineer's login is not detected (OD5; `actor_is_agent` undefined, R3.5.6).
   No agent in the JIT or PHI terminal (D2); incident-session flags (D3); normal-day domain review (OD9, OD10).
3. **Prod diff unseen on GitHub Team** unless the risk stop fires (⚠️ R4.6 #1). The stop misses
   approved malicious code (OD15) and has the OD18 limit; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8. One L3 approver (OD2).
4. **Admins can edit the gate:** logged, not prevented (📖 R3.2.2; ⚠️ R3.6 #1); UI changes to the
   `production` branch policy may leave no event (⚠️ R3.1.4).

**Evidence gaps** ([framework Gaps](01-framework.md#gaps-not-covered-or-only-as-an-open-item-in-work02-researchmd)):
change records, reconciliation, export and alerts arrive in Ph 2, so S3 and S8 are not routine
before then. Also G7, G8, G16, G18, G19, G17, G5; no CloudTrail chain or risk stop for k0s and
Firebase (G1, G2); Aurora SQL likely invisible to CloudTrail before activity streams (⚠️ R2.7.1).
Standards: ISO IDs, other jurisdictions and Papaya's sector under Decree 356 Art. 8 are open (R5.8);
the HIPAA proposed rule is not in force (📖 R5.3.1), so its items are forward-looking (⚠️ R5.7 #6).

**Open items, not decided in the framework:**

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| O-1 | Where JIT and real-data requests and approvals are stored (JIT tool not chosen, layer 1) |
| O-2 | Retention of raw logs, exports, telemetry and reports, and whether real-data approvals count as approval records (6 y); Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2) |
| O-3 | Who (Compliance, external auditors) can read the log archive and change records |
| O-4 | Destination and retention of the audit-log export and exported run logs (G7) |
| O-5 | Frequency of settings comparisons, machine sampling, digest validation, drift and non-prod scans |
| O-6 | Who performs the quarterly access review; where its record lives |
| O-7 | How on-call shifts and "primary unavailable" are recorded |
| O-8 | Telemetry backend for OTel |
| O-9 | Location and refresh cycle of the supplier register |

## Standards cross-reference

Mapping is inference (⚠️ R5.6). HIPAA and Vietnam text is documented (📖 R5.2, R5.4). ISO IDs are
recalled, not read (⚠️ R5.1): check them against Papaya's licensed copy or the NIST crosswalk (R5.8).

| Area (rows) | ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (⚠️ R5.1) | HIPAA Security Rule | Vietnam example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access, layers 1, 6 (C-01–C-03, C-15) | 5.15–5.18, 8.2, 8.3, 8.5 | 164.312(a)(2)(i) (📖 R5.2.6); 164.308(a)(3)–(4) (📖 R5.2.3, R5.2.4); 164.312(d) (📖 R5.2.8) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2) (📖 R5.4.3); Law 91 Art. 30(3) (📖 R5.4.7) |
| Change, layers 3, 5 (C-04–C-10, C-14) | 8.32, 8.31, 8.25, 5.3, 8.9, 8.4 | 164.312(c) (📖 R5.2.8); 164.316(b) (📖 R5.2.9); no change-approval standard exists (📖 R5.2.10) | — (none found; nearest Law 91 Art. 22, ⚠️ R5.6) |
| Suppliers and agent tools, layers 2, 4 (C-11–C-13) | 5.19–5.23, 8.19 | 164.308(b), 164.314(a) (📖 R5.6); workstations 164.310(b)–(d) (📖 R5.2.11; relevance ⚠️) | Law 91 Art. 20 (📖 R5.4.5); Decree 356 Arts. 10, 12 (📖 R5.4.7) |
| Data protection, layer 6 (C-15–C-18) | 5.12, 5.34, 8.11, 8.12, 8.33 | Minimum necessary, 164.502(b), Privacy Rule (📖 R1.11.1.8) | Decree 356 Art. 4(2); Law 91 Arts. 20, 22 (📖 R5.4.5) |
| Logging, break-glass, layer 7 (C-19–C-23) | 8.15, 8.16, 5.28, 5.33, 5.24–5.27 | 164.312(b) (📖 R5.2.7); 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) (📖 R5.2.2); 164.308(a)(6) (📖 R5.2.5); 164.312(a)(2)(ii) (📖 R5.2.6; mapping ⚠️ R5.7 #3) | Law 91 Art. 23, 72 h notice (📖 R5.4.6; mapping ⚠️); Decree 356 Art. 8(1), finance sector only (📖 R5.4.4; sector ⚠️) |
| Governance, layer 8 (C-24) | 5.2, 5.37, 6.3 | 164.308(a)(8) (📖 R5.2.10); 164.316(b) (📖 R5.2.9) | — |

"A named human approves" is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement
(⚠️ R5.7 #1). The record chain in this register is what shows Papaya follows its own policy.

# Examples

> Status: steps 1 (change workflow, layer 3) and 2 (identity and access, layer 1) reviewed in
> three rounds each; step 3 (agent runtime, supply chain, policy pack: E8–E10) reviewed in
> three rounds. · Updated: 2026-11-09

Concrete files behind [`../docs/01-framework.md`](../docs/01-framework.md). Each one exists to
prove one claim of the framework, and each has a local check. **Nothing here was run against
GitHub, AWS or any live system.** A passing check shows that the file says what the framework
says; it does not show that the platform enforces it. Every row lists what the check does
**not** prove.

Markers: ✅ checked in this repository's sessions (command output in the transcript) ·
📖 official documentation, linked · ⚠️ assumption, not verified · [design] proposal of this
submission, untested.

Placeholders: `example-org`, `<owner team>`, `123456` (app ID), `<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>`,
`<NONPROD_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>`, `<ORG_ID>`, `<REPO_ID>`, `<REVOKED_USER_ID_PLACEHOLDER>`. The monorepo
layout (`services/`, `infra/pulumi/`, `k8s/`, `web/`, `tools/`) is invented; Papaya's is unknown.

Where each file would live in the monorepo:

| Here | In the monorepo |
|---|---|
| `github/workflows/*.yml` | `.github/workflows/` |
| `github/CODEOWNERS` | `.github/CODEOWNERS` |
| `github/ruleset-main.json`, `github/environment-production/` | repository settings (REST API bodies), with an expected copy in git (layer 8) |
| `risk-stop/classify.py`, `risk-stop/adapters.py` | `tools/risk-stop/` |
| `risk-stop/deploy-approvals/<stack>/` | `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` at the root |
| `aws/oidc-trust-*.json` | trust policies of the deploy and preview roles, in the IAM stack (`infra/pulumi/iam/`) |
| `aws/scp-prod-ou.json` | the SCP stack (`infra/pulumi/org-scp/`, an L3 path), deployed from the management account |
| `aws/permission-set-prod-read-metadata.json` | the Identity Center stack (`infra/pulumi/iam/`) |
| `claude/managed-settings.phase*.json` | expected copy in git of the server-managed settings, which live in the Claude admin console (layer 2, layer 8) |
| `claude/marketplace/` | its own repository `example-org/claude-plugins`, with its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS (layer 5) |
| `pulumi-policy/` | `policy-packs/aws/` (an L3 path) |
| `risk-stop/fixtures/`, `tests/`, `schemas/`, `tools/`, `validate.sh` | only here, to check the examples |

## How to run

```bash
examples/validate.sh            # tools that are not installed are SKIPPED, and reported as such
ACTIONLINT=/path/actionlint ZIZMOR=/path/zizmor examples/validate.sh
```

Needs Python 3 with `jsonschema`, `PyYAML` and `git`; optional `jq`, `yamllint`, `shellcheck`,
`actionlint`, `zizmor`, `claude` (for `claude plugin validate`), and Node.js with
`npm ci` run once in `pulumi-policy/` (downloads packages; `node_modules/` is not committed).
Tests use the standard `unittest`.

## What each file proves

| # | Files | Proves (framework) | Checked by | Does not prove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | [`github/ruleset-main.json`](github/ruleset-main.json) | The approval gate is the merge to `main` (layer 3, ADR-0003): PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, stale approvals dismissed, approval by someone other than the last pusher, branch up to date (no merge queue), required checks pinned to a source app, no force push or deletion, empty bypass list | JSON Schema of the create-ruleset request body; key-by-path check; design tests | That GitHub enforces it. `approval-gate` comes from a dedicated app whose ID (`123456`) is a placeholder (gap G19). The other checks are pinned to GitHub Actions (ID 15368 ✅ `GET https://api.github.com/apps/github-actions`), so any workflow in the repo can likely post a check with the same name (⚠️ layer 3, G19) |
| E2 | [`github/CODEOWNERS`](github/CODEOWNERS) | L3 process paths: owned by the L3 owner team only; deployable paths: co-owned by the domain team and the on-call group, so one approval from either satisfies code-owner review (OD9, OD13; 📖 R3.2.7); risk-stop approvals: co-owned by the stack's owners and on-call (OD8). Fail-safe default so no file is unowned [design] | Effective owners resolved with GitHub's "last matching pattern takes the most precedence" (📖 [about code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)); every stack in `deploy-on-main.yml` checked for code and approvals owners | That the teams exist and have write access: GitHub drops such owners silently. [`codeowners-validate.yml`](github/workflows/codeowners-validate.yml) covers that in a real repo |
| E3 | [`github/workflows/`](github/workflows/) | "Merge approval = deploy approval" (layer 3): only the reusable [`deploy-prod.yml`](github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml) uses `production`; no ref/SHA input; no `workflow_dispatch`, `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run`; one concurrency group per stack, running deploys never cancelled; only the current tip of `main` is deployed (no re-run of an old run) [design]; preview → risk stop → apply, and the stop cannot be skipped, ignored or bypassed by an `if:`; apply commands use only allowed flags. Layer 5: OIDC, per-job permissions, SHA-pinned actions; `npm ci`, Pulumi plugins and the policy pack installed before the AWS credentials are in the job (the Serverless framework download: ⚠️ assumed to happen at `serverless --version`); this does not keep install scripts away from the job's OIDC token (Limits). PRs preview non-prod only | `actionlint`, `zizmor --persona=auditor`, `yamllint`; design tests (`test_workflow_policy.py`) | That the workflows run: the Pulumi/Serverless steps were never executed. The tests see only these files, not a whole monorepo |
| E3b | [`github/environment-production/`](github/environment-production/) | `production` accepts deployments from `main` only and has no required reviewers (not available on GitHub Team for private repos, R3.1.2); names of the k0s/Firebase exception secrets (OD1, OD6) and of the prod variables | JSON Schemas of the two request bodies (environment PUT, branch-policy POST); key-by-path check; design tests | That GitHub applies it; admins can still change or delete the environment (layer 7 compares live settings) |
| E4 | [`aws/oidc-trust-prod-deploy.json`](aws/oidc-trust-prod-deploy.json), [`aws/oidc-trust-nonprod-preview.json`](aws/oidc-trust-nonprod-preview.json) | Layer 1 "CI → AWS", ADR-0008: the prod deploy role trusts only the `production` environment of the monorepo; PRs get only a non-prod role in the non-prod account. Immutable subject format with owner and repository IDs (📖 R3.4.4; environment form ⚠️ R3.7 A2); `aud` = `sts.amazonaws.com` (📖 R3.4.1); `StringEquals` only. No `sts:TagSession`: the action does not tag sessions with OIDC (📖 `configure-aws-credentials` README at the pinned SHA). **Prerequisite:** repositories created before 2026-07-15 keep the old subject format unless the organization or repository opts in (📖 R3.4.4); Papaya's monorepo likely needs that opt-in first, or every deploy is refused. Optional narrowing with `job_workflow_ref` (⚠️ G10). The same trust applies to both prod deploy roles (Pulumi and Serverless) | Design tests | That AWS accepts the policy. `environment:production` alone does not say which branch: the environment's branch rule (E3b) does (⚠️ R3.4.3) |
| E5 | [`aws/scp-prod-ou.json`](aws/scp-prod-ou.json) (phase 2) | Layer 1 SCPs: Lambda code/config changes only by CloudFormation deployment roles, the **Pulumi** prod deploy role and JIT roles (the Serverless deploy role is not exempt: it only passes the CloudFormation role); claim-data reads only by application and approved data-read roles; the names of exempt roles can be created or changed only by the IAM stack's (Pulumi) deploy role; pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:UserId` (📖 R2.4.4); no tampering with trails in prod accounts. Deny-only; condition keys from R2.3.8. The outside-org write deny (all OUs) is not in this file | Every action exists in the AWS catalogue; size ≤ 10,240 characters minified and as written (📖 R2.3.4); exempt principals, protected role names and trail actions pinned exactly by the tests; claim-data reads checked to include a shared list | How it evaluates with other SCPs. Role names `cfn-deployment-*`, `github-prod-deploy-pulumi`, `app-claims-*` and permission sets `InfraOperator-<service>`, `DataRead-<store>` are [design] names. Identity Center role ARNs have a region segment except when the identity source is in us-east-1, and end in `AWSReservedSSO_<set>_<suffix>` (📖 [referencing permission sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/referencingpermissionsets.html)); both forms are listed. The data-read action list is partial (G13) |
| E6 | [`aws/permission-set-prod-read-metadata.json`](aws/permission-set-prod-read-metadata.json) | Layer 1, ADR-0002: `ProdReadMetadata` reads metrics and metadata; 1-hour session (📖 R2.1.4); raw logs and function configuration only for named services that are redacted or use runtime secrets. Reads that expose configuration, data or secrets are left out (finding 11) | Wildcards expanded with the AWS catalogue; no action AWS marks as a write or permission-management action; no known data read; `Resource: "*"` only for an explicit, reviewed allowlist of metadata actions in the test (no wildcards; AWS's `IsList` is not trusted, finding 12); log and config reads only on one named log group or function each. An action missing from the catalogue fails the test (add its service to `tools/fetch_aws_actions.py`) | Only the **listed** data reads are known to be absent (G13). The file follows the shapes of `CreatePermissionSet` and `PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet` (⚠️ field names from memory) |
| E7 | [`risk-stop/`](risk-stop/) | The risk stop (layer 3, ADR-0004) can be built: risky prod diffs stop the deploy (per category, for Pulumi and CloudFormation types alike, plus property names on any type); an approval counts only for the exact preview, only if it was merged to `main` on its own after the stopped commit, never edited, and the stack's code is unchanged since the stopped commit; approvals expire 7 days after they were merged; the summary shows which resources and properties change, never values; unreadable input stops | 25 unit tests; approval tests run against throwaway git repositories, including the bypasses found in review (edited approval, merge-commit PR, approval on a side branch, approval merged before a change inside the stack, runtime edit of the file) and one test that documents a gap that stays open (see Limits) | ⚠️ The JSON shapes of `pulumi preview --json` and `serverless diff --json` are **assumed** ([`adapters.py`](risk-stop/adapters.py)). That a real preview gives the same hash twice for unchanged code (Options §8). See "Limits of the risk stop" |
| E8 | [`claude/managed-settings.phase1.json`](claude/managed-settings.phase1.json), [`claude/managed-settings.phase2.json`](claude/managed-settings.phase2.json) | Layer 2, ADR-0007, phases of layer 8 and OD4: phase 1 holds exactly the layer-8 subset (Manual default with auto mode kept, D1; bypass off; an allowlist of two exact repo scripts, `npm test` and `npm run lint`, OD7b, finding 19; `Read(~/.aws/**)` denied and `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` (owner decision OD21); plugin and MCP catalogue locks; claude.ai connectors off; telemetry on with every content flag `0`; version floor 2.1.248). Phase 2 is Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json` (✅ fetched at commit `9196319`). **Kept from the template:** provider and login lock, managed-only rules/hooks, shell allow rules that do not skip the auto-mode classifier (`classifyAllShell`), the auto-mode `"$defaults"` pins, the template's credential denies. **Papaya's deviations**, each listed in [E8: deviations from the HIPAA template](#e8-deviations-from-the-hipaa-template): credential denies extended to the stack (AWS, GitHub, GCP, Firebase, Docker, kube, Pulumi, Serverless); sandbox with `aws *`/`pulumi *`/`serverless *` excluded plus matching `ask` rules, so they always prompt (refused in `dontAsk`; bypass is off); `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true` (OD12), so sandboxed commands are auto-approved in auto mode too and for them the sandbox, not the classifier, is the control (📖 sandboxing, README-hipaa); managed-only mods; version floor 2.1.310 | Community JSON Schema from schemastore.org (not an Anthropic source) plus the key-by-path check; keys and tool names the schema lacks need a documentation source (📖, listed in the test); design tests | That Claude Code enforces it: the live copy is edited in the admin console and compared monthly (layer 2, G18). On laptops without MDM a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7); `forceLoginMethod`, `forceLoginOrgUUID` and `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` only hold from the first start if delivered by MDM, because server-managed settings arrive after the first sign-in (📖 [iam](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam.md), [settings reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md#forceremotesettingsrefresh)). `excludedCommands` from a user's `~/.claude/settings.json` and from `--settings` still apply: no managed-only lock covers that list (📖 settings reference). An excluded CLI runs code from the repository outside the sandbox (`pulumi` runs the stack program, `serverless` its config and plugins), and a sandboxed command can write that code without a prompt (OD12); the prompt then shows only `pulumi preview` (📖 sandboxing, `excludedCommands` warning) [limit, accepted in layer 2]. Sandboxed reads are a denylist: anything in the home folder not listed is readable without a prompt, and can leave through any allowed domain, e.g. a push to another GitHub repository (📖 sandboxing, "Security limitations"); Linear/Slack tokens and key files that `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` or `KUBECONFIG` point to elsewhere are not listed (⚠️). MCP entries and network domains are placeholders (G9); the `npx -y <pkg>@<version>` pin fixes the top-level package only, its dependencies float [limit] |
| E9 | [`claude/marketplace/`](claude/marketplace/) | Layer 4, ADR-0006: the plugin catalogue is a private marketplace; every third-party source pinned to a commit (`sha`, 📖 [marketplace reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/marketplace-reference.md)); one review record per entry, with the layer-4 checklist ([`reviews/`](claude/marketplace/reviews/)) | `claude plugin validate` (✅ Claude Code 2.1.319: it fails on an invalid entry, e.g. a missing `repo` or a malformed `sha`); tests that every external source is pinned (`sha`; for npm a bare package name with an exact `version` and no own `registry`; or `sha256`), no `command` source, and every third-party entry has a review record | `claude plugin validate` accepts an unpinned `github` source and a `command` source (✅ mutation), hence the separate pin test. Plugin contents were not reviewed: the vendors and SHAs are placeholders |
| E10 | [`pulumi-policy/`](pulumi-policy/) (phase 2) | Layer 5, OD8: mandatory Pulumi Policies (formerly CrossGuard, 📖 R4.2.1) that stop a deploy on an IAM `Allow` with `*`, `<service>:*` (also spelled with `?`, 📖 [IAM Action element](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_action.html)), `NotAction` or any wildcard in an `iam`/`sts`/`organizations`/`sso`/`identitystore` action, in a managed, role, user or group policy or a role's inline policy; on attaching `AdministratorAccess`, `PowerUserAccess` or any AWS managed `*FullAccess` policy by these routes (the three attachment types, `PolicyAttachment`, the three `*PolicyAttachmentsExclusive` types, `Role.managedPolicyArns`); on an RDS/Aurora cluster without deletion protection; on an S3 public access block with any flag off | `tsc` on the pack, then 35 cases that call each check with hand-made properties and a minimal stand-in for the CLI's arguments (`isType`), with no Pulumi engine and no cloud; type tokens ✅ against `@pulumi/aws` 7.51.1 | Not covered: Identity Center permission sets (`aws:ssoadmin/*`), admin-equivalent names outside the list (e.g. `AdministratorAccess-Amplify`), RDS instances and global clusters, the account-level S3 public access block; and Serverless stacks, which are not Pulumi (layer 5). Retiring a cluster needs an exception (comment in `policies.ts`). A value unknown during preview (e.g. a policy built with `pulumi.jsonStringify` from a resource of the same update) turns the check into `advisory` for that preview (✅ `@pulumi/policy` 1.21.0 `server.js`); the stop then comes during `pulumi up`, possibly after earlier resources were created (⚠️ not run). Access Analyzer (layer 5) is the preview-time check. Customer-managed policies made outside the stack are not checked. The S3 rule checks only `BucketPublicAccessBlock` resources, not that every claim bucket has one |


The AWS action catalogue in [`schemas/aws-actions.json`](schemas/aws-actions.json) is taken from AWS's
machine-readable Service Authorization Reference (✅ `https://servicereference.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/`,
fetched 2026-11-09, 22 services) by [`tools/fetch_aws_actions.py`](tools/fetch_aws_actions.py).
Mutation runs ✅ for E4–E6 (all made the tests fail): `logs:Get*` or `s3:Get*` on `*`; a misspelled
action; a write action; `StringLike` on the subject; the old subject format; an 8-hour session;
an `Allow` in the SCP.

Schemas in [`schemas/`](schemas/) are extracted from GitHub's REST OpenAPI description
(`github/rest-api-description` at commit `2f8f80e47ea4d3292cf4e37ba9d9b25475e06140`, OpenAPI 3.0.3 ✅)
by [`tools/extract_github_schemas.py`](tools/extract_github_schemas.py), which resolves `$ref` and
`nullable`. They do not forbid unknown keys, so a misspelled key passes schema validation; the
key-by-path check ([`tests/schema_keys.py`](tests/schema_keys.py)) catches it (✅ mutation run:
`require_last_pusher_approval` passes the schema and is reported by the key check).

Mutation runs ✅ (each must make the tests fail, and did): `continue-on-error: true` on the risk
stop; `|| true` after the classifier; `if: always() && …` on an apply step; `pulumi up -f`;
a non-"Apply" step running `pulumi up` with `if: failure()`; `exit 1` replaced by `true` in the
tip-of-`main` guard; the guard reading `commits/main` instead of `git/ref/heads/main`; removing
the "approval merged on main's first-parent history" check;
removing the CODEOWNERS line for `deploy-approvals/claims-api/`; a broad CODEOWNERS line after
the L3 section.

Mutation runs ✅ for E8–E10 (each made the tests fail): an `excludedCommands` entry without ` *`;
`Bash(git log *)` in the phase-1 allowlist; `~/.config/gh` removed from the sandbox credentials;
`autoMode.classifyAllShell` off; an MCP allowlist entry with two keys; `computer-use` removed from
`deniedMcpServers`; a phase-2 key added to phase 1; an unpinned plugin source; a policy set to
`advisory`; the `UserPolicy` check, the `Role.managedPolicyArns` check, the `iam`/`sts` wildcard
rule or the `*FullAccess` match removed from the policy pack. Round 2 of the review found mutations the tests missed (an emptied `hard_deny`, a `*` domain, emptied `denyWrite`, an extra package in an MCP command, an npm `package` with its own version), and round 3 more (a template env var or deny rule removed, `Read(~/.kube/**)` narrowed to one file, `autoMode.allow` without `"$defaults"`, an `allowRead` entry, `*:*` in a policy); each now fails a test.

Phase 2 starts from Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json` (📖 [README-hipaa](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/examples/settings/README-hipaa.md)).
Every key of the template is kept as written except these:

| Template key | Phase 2 | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `permissions.deny` `WebFetch` | moved to `ask` | Engineers read vendor docs during work; each fetch is approved instead (layer 2) [design] |
| `permissions.deny`, `sandbox.credentials`, `filesystem.denyWrite` | extended | Papaya's stack adds `~/.aws` (whole folder, incl. the SSO cache), `~/.config/gcloud`, Firebase CLI token (⚠️ path `~/.config/configstore/firebase-tools.json` not checked), `~/.docker/config.json`, `~/.kube`, `~/.pulumi`; `~/.config/gh` also hidden from the sandbox (finding 20); `~/.serverlessrc` (⚠️ path not checked); env vars `PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE`, `FIREBASE_TOKEN`, `SERVERLESS_ACCESS_KEY` (⚠️ names not checked) |
| `strictKnownMarketplaces: []` | the private marketplace repository | The catalogue (layer 4, ADR-0006) |
| `allowedMcpServers: []` | catalogue entries | Same; placeholders (G9) |
| `deniedMcpServers` `ide` | not denied | The IDE bridge (VS Code, JetBrains) is local and is how most engineers use Claude Code; cost of denying it is losing editor integration. `claude-in-chrome` and `computer-use` stay denied: built-in servers are exempt from `allowedMcpServers`, only the denylist reaches them (📖 settings reference, `allowedMcpServers`) |

README-hipaa says to keep the key when `disableAutoMode` is set, which is D1's fallback: set it then |
| `sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly: true` | not set | It only filters `allowRead`, which managed settings do not use here, and while set, `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` does not reach sandboxed commands (📖 settings reference). The docs' pattern `denyRead: ["~/"]` + `allowRead` for the work folders would close the denylist gap but needs a fixed repository location on every laptop (open item for layer 2). Accepted limit, like user `excludedCommands`: a developer's own `allowRead` entry merges and can re-open part of a denied path (📖 sandboxing, "Keep developers from widening the policy"; whether a `credentials.files` deny still holds then: ⚠️) |
| `env` proxy variables | not set | No egress proxy at Papaya is known; sandboxed commands go through the sandbox's own network allowlist |
| `network.allowedDomains` | GitHub, npm, PyPI (placeholders) | Papaya's registries (G9) |
| — | added (diff against the template): `requiredMinimumVersion`, `permissions.defaultMode`, `permissions.allow`, `permissions.ask` (WebFetch and the three excluded CLIs), `blockedMarketplaces`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, `pluginConfigs` (managed-only mods), `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true` (OD12), `sandbox.excludedCommands`, `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead`. Costs engineers will notice, and the workaround (most from README-hipaa, "What developers lose"):

- Inside the sandbox, `git fetch`/`pull`/`push` to the private monorepo, `gh`, and `npm ci` from a
  private registry fail: SSH keys, git credentials, `~/.npmrc`, the GitHub token variables and the
  `gh` configuration are hidden. The engineer runs these at the `!` prompt, outside Claude's tools;
  the agent cannot push or open the pull request itself.
- Docker and Testcontainers fail (`allowAllUnixSockets: false`); on macOS, servers on localhost
  cannot be started or reached (`allowLocalBinding: false`), git over SSH and Go-based CLIs fail TLS
  (📖 sandboxing, troubleshooting). Such tests run at the `!` prompt or in CI.
- `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`: Claude Code does not start when the settings cannot be fetched
  (`claude auth` still works). `failIfUnavailable`: Claude Code does not start on native Windows
  (no sandbox there; WSL2 works) (📖 sandboxing).
- `/goal` is gone under `allowManagedHooksOnly` (README-hipaa); `cleanupPeriodDays: 30` deletes
  local transcripts after 30 days; every `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` call prompts, in auto mode too (`ask` rules; the managed-only rule lock hides "always allow").

  `.claude/skills/*/.claude-plugin/` from loading; plain `SKILL.md` skills still load (📖 [plugins for
  organizations](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/org.md)).
- `forceLoginMethod: claudeai` pre-selects but does not enforce the method on the interactive login
  screen, so a Console login is still possible there (📖 iam); `allowedHttpHookUrls` merges entries
  from a developer's own settings, and `allowManagedHooksOnly` is what decides which hooks run
