# ADR-0007: Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-09
- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-6, Options §0.4; D1, D3; OD4, OD7b, OD12)
- **Scope:** Claude Code on laptops (server-managed settings, Team plan) and in CI

## 1. Context

The brief names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem. It is tempting to make Claude Code
settings the main control. But server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not a security
boundary" (📖 R1.1.7), local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8), Bash rules are not a boundary
(📖 R1.2.6), and on laptops without MDM another login or provider skips server-managed settings
(📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11).

## 2. Options considered

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Today (brief): some engineers turn prompts off; no organization policy is described (P3c) | No friction | Prompts turned off unnoticed; no evidence |
| A. Settings as the boundary (lock everything, block auto mode) | Simple story | Bypassable on laptops; high friction; people work around it |
| B. Settings as hygiene; IAM and the CI gate as the boundary | Boundary holds even if settings are bypassed | Settings give weaker guarantees than they appear to |

## 3. Decision

Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
uniform defaults:

- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` in
  `sandbox.excludedCommands` [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).

Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).

Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).

## 4. Consequences

- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read AWS PHI
  stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write is removed (PHI paths outside IAM
  are process-only, ADR-0009). Compliance gets
  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference): repo code that the agent can edit (Pulumi programs, Serverless
  plugins) then runs with network and `~/.aws`, and SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by
  ADR-0002. With OD12, Manual mode does not mean a prompt for every command (📖 R5.5.5b).
- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.

## Independent review: README, engineer guide, diagrams, whole-repo checks

I edited no repo files. Scratch output is in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/6db3dd9e-1a2b-4563-ab89-a7de7a1f8366/scratchpad/review-final-b/ (rendered PNG/SVG files, `linkcheck.py`, `changes.txt`).

### Checks run (✅)
- **Links:** `linkcheck.py` checked README.md, docs/*.md, docs/adr/*.md, diagrams/README.md and examples/README.md (20 files). It follows relative targets and resolves #anchors with GitHub slug rules (link text used inside headings, fenced code skipped). Result: **0 broken links**. I also tested the checker on a copy with a deliberately broken anchor and a missing file, and it caught both.
- **Secrets and personal data:** I scanned `git diff HEAD` plus all untracked files except transcripts/ for 12-digit account IDs, emails, AWS/GitHub/Slack/Anthropic/Google key patterns, PEM headers, real-account ARNs, `secret=`-style assignments and home paths. **0 hits.** Two items were already committed before this change: the author's own name in the transcript path (README:81) and the public challenge URL. Both are covered by the Rule 2 exception.
- **Diagrams:** I rendered all three with `mmdc -w 1400`. All render, and nothing is clipped. The committed SVGs carry the same text labels as fresh renders (md5 of the sorted labels matches), so they are up to date with the `.mmd` sources.
- **README length:** 677 words before the Transcripts section, under the ~700 target. **Guide:** 1,095 words.
- **Term consistency:** these terms are used the same way across README, guide, framework, rollout plan, register and diagrams: incident responder, on-call approver, on-call group, L3 owner team, L0–L3, L3-JIT, L3-data, phases 1–3, OD1–OD21, G1–G20, S1–S11, E1–E10. No reference points to an ID that does not exist.

### HIGH

**H1. README:62-63 and README:72-73: the claim about permission mode and profile is contradicted by the transcripts.**
- *Claim:* "From session 2 on, sessions ran in the default (Manual) permission mode with a clean config profile". Also: "Session 1 used the default profile; later sessions use a clean profile."
- *Evidence from the session log:* work/session-log.md:52-55 says session 2 ran in the VS Code extension with `--permission-mode=auto` on the default `~/.claude` profile, and that this was accepted.
- *Evidence from the transcripts (✅ `grep -o '"permissionMode":"…"'` over the transcript `.jsonl` files):*
  - Clean profile, recorded as `auto` only: 28544ac2 (session 3), 2e770088, 35d024b5, 3695394c, and the current session 6db3dd9e.
  - Clean profile, recorded as `default`: only the short sessions a95ee902, 2e7942e6 and 92572efd.
  - Default profile: three sessions (6cd4c971, 206fa37f, a41c0cff), all recorded as `auto`.
- *Caveat (⚠️):* I am reading the `permissionMode` field as the mode in effect at each turn. My own subagent context also says auto mode is active.
- *Effect:* the graded transcripts disprove the "How this was built" claim, and the README uses that claim as evidence that "the transcripts show the prompts the framework asks engineers to accept". The same decision is also stated in CLAUDE.md ("Permission mode", "Clean config directory").
- *Fix:* say what actually happened. Manual mode was the plan from session 2, but most working sessions ran in auto mode (the VS Code default). Give the reason, record the deviation as accepted, and correct which sessions used which profile. The owner has to decide the wording; the CLAUDE.md decision line should be corrected at the same time.

### MEDIUM

**M1. README:61: "Rounds and owner decisions are in work/session-log.md" is not true yet.**
- The log ends at "Bước 3 (E8–E10)". It has nothing on the framework trim, the rollout plan, the register, the guide, the README, the diagrams or their review rounds.
- Its English summary (lines 3-13) stops at the 2026-11-09 options work. A reader without Vietnamese sees no review round from the framework onward, which breaks CLAUDE.md Rule 3 (the summary must restate the note).
- *Fix:* add entries for these steps and extend the English summary.

**M2. README:17 and the table at README:21-22: "Nobody … holds … long-lived credentials" leaves out the k0s/Firebase exception.**
- The owner approved an exception for k0s/Firebase CI deploy credentials (framework §1 table, line 47; OD1, OD6; layer 5). The shortfall paragraph doesn't mention it either.
- *Fix:* add "except owner-approved k0s/Firebase CI deploy credentials, stored as `production` environment secrets (OD1)".

**M3. README:24-27: the shortfall section leaves out material items from framework §1 (lines 51-85).**
- Missing:
  - admins can edit the gate (logged, not prevented, and an admin's agent can do the same);
  - L3 changes get one approver;
  - the on-call group can approve any domain's PR on a normal day, so domain review there is only a process rule;
  - if the required-check app is down, all merges are blocked;
  - whether HIPAA applies is a legal question.
- A compliance reader would expect at least the first two.
- *Fix:* add one short clause each for "admins can edit the gate" and "one approver at L3". Otherwise, say "four of nine; the full list is in §1".

**M4. README:19-22: the README shows only what Engineering gains, not what it costs.**
- Costs the framework states:
  - the incident lane is slower (an estimated 11–46 min against 2–20 min today, layer 7);
  - raw logs and configuration are not readable during the transition, called "the largest cost of the first months" (layer 1);
  - more prompts;
  - from phase 2 the sandbox breaks `git push`, `gh` and Docker;
  - 24/7 approver duty, with two people awake at night (§1);
  - up to 5 days to get a new tool approved.
- The brief and CLAUDE.md ask for every control's cost to engineers.
- *Fix:* add a one-line "What it costs engineers" row.

**M5. docs/02-engineer-guide.md:51 and diagrams/01-change-workflow.mmd:11 overstate who approves a normal PR.**
- Both say a normal domain PR is approved by "your domain team, or the on-call group".
- The OD9 process rule (framework 340-342) says otherwise: a group member approves another domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and they are on shift, and a monthly report counts the exceptions.
- *Fix:* add that limit in both places.

**M6. The guide has no section for engineers who are on the on-call approver rota.**
- What they need to know (framework Roles table line 102, §1 lines 71-73, layer 7):
  - 24/7 duty, with an approval wait of ≤ 15 min (S7);
  - while on call they only approve: no fix, no JIT request;
  - primary approves, backup only replaces an unavailable primary;
  - the cross-domain rule from M5;
  - a night incident needs two people awake.
- This is the largest new duty for engineers, and only the incident-responder side is described.
- *Fix:* add a short "When you are the on-call approver" section.

**M7. Guide §1 (lines 25-29) leaves out phase-2 changes engineers will notice, and one sentence is unconditional.**
- Missing:
  - `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`: an engineer's own and the project's allow rules are ignored, so prompts likely rise (framework 205);
  - sign-in is locked to Papaya's org, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` sessions are refused (framework 209);
  - a minimum version floor;
  - a prompt for every WebFetch;
  - native Windows does not start, and on macOS localhost servers fail (examples/README 120-128).
- Line 28, "Each `aws`, `pulumi` or `serverless` call asks you first", only holds from phase 2 (the `ask` rules are in E8 phase 2). In phase 1 these calls run without a prompt in auto mode.
- *Fix:* add a short cost list and add "from phase 2, in auto mode too" to that sentence.

**M8. Guide §2, §4 and §5 leave out an action engineers must take.**
- Engineers must end the portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant (framework layer 2, lines 228-230). This protects the riskiest window against token theft.
- *Fix:* add it to the JIT and real-data steps.

**M9. Guide:13 and guide:95 make wrong statements about non-prod data.**
- "Non-prod is yours … no new approval" and "Non-prod holds no real data" are wrong during the transition. Stores not yet scanned follow the L3-data rule and are not part of the free loop (framework §1 line 46, layer 6 lines 579-581).
- "If you find some, report it" is a rule the framework does not contain.
- *Fix:* restate the unscanned-store rule and drop the new rule, or cite a source for it.

**M10. diagrams/02-identity-trust-boundaries.mmd:39-41 shows things the text doesn't say.**
- The `PROD → CT` edge says "every API call". The text says data events are on only for PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS, and that Aurora SQL is likely invisible (framework 608-617).
- `DEP -->|apply| DATA` suggests the deploy role writes claim data. It changes resources, not data.
- The GitHub audit-log export is drawn inside the log-archive account. Its destination is still open (register O-4), and the export starts in phase 2.
- *Fix:* relabel to "management events + selected data events", point the deploy edge at "prod resources", and mark the export destination as open.

### LOW
- **Guide:112:** CLAUDE.md changes are approved "by the L3 owner team, not only your domain team". It should say the L3 owner team *only*; a domain-team approval doesn't count (framework 297, 308-309).
- **Guide:57-58, risk-stop approval PR:**
  - By default the first approver approves it; another owner makes three people and is recorded as a deviation (OD13, OD11). The guide's "may be" understates this.
  - "If prod has not changed" should be "if the new prod preview hash matches".
  - Missing cost: later merges to the same stack stop too.
- **Guide:68-69:** "no web access" overstates it. The session has no WebFetch, but Bash can still reach the network. Give the real command: `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"` in an empty scratch directory (framework 247).
- **Guide:75:** "11–46 min end to end" should be "from decision to apply" (work/03-options.md:395).
- **Guide:80:** "a job compares your commands with CloudTrail". In phase 1 this is done by hand (rollout 1.13); it is automated in phase 2 (2.3).
- **Guide §5:** missing:
  - a store holding PHI is treated as PHI unless the agent reads a view without PHI;
  - one tenant per grant, and nothing posted to shared places after reading a tenant's data (layer 6);
  - "or de-identify first" for partner documents.
- **Guide §4:** missing:
  - a risky change already waiting on `main` blocks the fix for that stack;
  - at night, process paths wait for the L3 owner team, or the JIT fallback is used.
- **README:15-16:** add "during an incident" to the JIT fallback (framework 644: incidents only).
- **README:22:** "retrievable in ≤ 30 min" is the S8 target, and it is realistic only from phase 2 (register, "Evidence for one prod change").
- **README:58-61:** the reviewer claim doesn't match the log.
  - Framing (work/01) was reviewed with the owner in grill-me rounds, not by an independent reviewer (session-log 58-68).
  - The options review was stopped by the agent after a grep-only check (session-log 77-79).
  - In practice most design steps ended with the owner stopping the rounds and the last fixes not re-reviewed.
  - *Fix:* reword to match.
- **README:67:** "hooks are advisory (ADR-0007)". ADR-0007 doesn't mention hooks. Cite framework layer 2, line 258 ("hooks fail open unless `onFailure: block`", R1.5.2), or say "agent-side controls are hygiene (ADR-0007)".
- **README:6:** status "complete for review" while docs/04-compliance-mapping.md:3 is still "draft for owner review".
- **Diagram 01:**
  - The L0 branch is labelled "Non-prod roles or PR pipeline", but L0 also covers prod metadata reads with the read-only identity (framework 294).
  - The "hash differs → stops again" edge from RE is missing (framework 353-354).
  - The process-path list leaves out `tools/risk-stop/` and the policy packs.
- **Diagram 02, layout:**
  - The "approved PR" edge from Engineer crosses the agent box.
  - The labels "GitHub OIDC, no stored keys" and "every API call" sit on subgraph borders.
  - JIT and DataRead are drawn from the Engineer only. The text says the shared SSO cache could reach them, with only process rule D2 preventing it (framework 226-228); a label saying so would be more accurate.
- **Diagram 03:** the JIT fallback is drawn as if it follows the PR path. Use an `alt`/`else` block. Also, "for 1 h" is the role session; the real window is up to about 2 h (framework 647).

### Engineering and compliance lenses
- **Engineer:** the guide clearly explains shipping, incidents and the cost of losing raw logs. It does not cover being on the approver rota, the phase-2 laptop changes, or the unscanned-store exception (M6–M9).
- **Compliance:** the README shortfall section is accurate but incomplete (M2, M3). The "How this was built" section currently contains a claim the transcripts disprove (H1).

## Independent review: README, engineer guide, diagrams, whole-repo checks

I edited no repo files. Scratch output is in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-do-hoang-minh-hung-papaya-devsecops-challenge/6db3dd9e-1a2b-4563-ab89-a7de7a1f8366/scratchpad/review-final-b/ (rendered PNG/SVG files, `linkcheck.py`, `changes.txt`).

### Checks run (✅)
- **Links:** `linkcheck.py` checked README.md, docs/*.md, docs/adr/*.md, diagrams/README.md and examples/README.md (20 files). It follows relative targets and resolves #anchors with GitHub slug rules (link text used inside headings, fenced code skipped). Result: **0 broken links**. I also tested the checker on a copy with a deliberately broken anchor and a missing file, and it caught both.
- **Secrets and personal data:** I scanned `git diff HEAD` plus all untracked files except transcripts/ for 12-digit account IDs, emails, AWS/GitHub/Slack/Anthropic/Google key patterns, PEM headers, real-account ARNs, `secret=`-style assignments and home paths. **0 hits.** Two items were already committed before this change: the author's own name in the transcript path (README:81) and the public challenge URL. Both are covered by the Rule 2 exception.
- **Diagrams:** I rendered all three with `mmdc -w 1400`. All render, and nothing is clipped. The committed SVGs carry the same text labels as fresh renders (md5 of the sorted labels matches), so they are up to date with the `.mmd` sources.

- **Term consistency:** these terms are used the same way across README, guide, framework, rollout plan, register and diagrams: incident responder, on-call approver, on-call group, L3 owner team, L0–L3, L3-JIT, L3-data, phases 1–3, OD1–OD21, G1–G20, S1–S11, E1–E10. No reference points to an ID that does not exist.

### HIGH

**H1. README:62-63 and README:72-73: the claim about permission mode and profile is contradicted by the transcripts.**
- *Claim:* "From session 2 on, sessions ran in the default (Manual) permission mode with a clean config profile". Also: "Session 1 used the default profile; later sessions use a clean profile."
- *Evidence from the session log:* work/session-log.md:52-55 says session 2 ran in the VS Code extension with `--permission-mode=auto` on the default `~/.claude` profile, and that this was accepted.
- *Evidence from the transcripts (✅ `grep -o '"permissionMode":"…"'` over the transcript `.jsonl` files):*
  - Clean profile, recorded as `auto` only: 28544ac2 (session 3), 2e770088, 35d024b5, 3695394c, and the current session 6db3dd9e.
  - Clean profile, recorded as `default`: only the short sessions a95ee902, 2e7942e6 and 92572efd.
  - Default profile: three sessions (6cd4c971, 206fa37f, a41c0cff), all recorded as `auto`.
- *Caveat (⚠️):* I am reading the `permissionMode` field as the mode in effect at each turn. My own subagent context also says auto mode is active.
- *Effect:* the graded transcripts disprove the "How this was built" claim, and the README uses that claim as evidence that "the transcripts show the prompts the framework asks engineers to accept". The same decision is also stated in CLAUDE.md ("Permission mode", "Clean config directory").
- *Fix:* say what actually happened. Manual mode was the plan from session 2, but most working sessions ran in auto mode (the VS Code default). Give the reason, record the deviation as accepted, and correct which sessions used which profile. The owner has to decide the wording; the CLAUDE.md decision line should be corrected at the same time.

### MEDIUM

**M1. README:61: "Rounds and owner decisions are in work/session-log.md" is not true yet.**
- The log ends at "Bước 3 (E8–E10)". It has nothing on the framework trim, the rollout plan, the register, the guide, the README, the diagrams or their review rounds.
- Its English summary (lines 3-13) stops at the 2026-11-09 options work. A reader without Vietnamese sees no review round from the framework onward, which breaks CLAUDE.md Rule 3 (the summary must restate the note).
- *Fix:* add entries for these steps and extend the English summary.

**M2. README:17 and the table at README:21-22: "Nobody … holds … long-lived credentials" leaves out the k0s/Firebase exception.**
- The owner approved an exception for k0s/Firebase CI deploy credentials (framework §1 table, line 47; OD1, OD6; layer 5). The shortfall paragraph doesn't mention it either.
- *Fix:* add "except owner-approved k0s/Firebase CI deploy credentials, stored as `production` environment secrets (OD1)".

**M3. README:24-27: the shortfall section leaves out material items from framework §1 (lines 51-85).**
- Missing:
  - admins can edit the gate (logged, not prevented, and an admin's agent can do the same);
  - L3 changes get one approver;
  - the on-call group can approve any domain's PR on a normal day, so domain review there is only a process rule;
  - if the required-check app is down, all merges are blocked;
  - whether HIPAA applies is a legal question.
- A compliance reader would expect at least the first two.
- *Fix:* add one short clause each for "admins can edit the gate" and "one approver at L3". Otherwise, say "four of nine; the full list is in §1".

**M4. README:19-22: the README shows only what Engineering gains, not what it costs.**
- Costs the framework states:
  - the incident lane is slower (an estimated 11–46 min against 2–20 min today, layer 7);
  - raw logs and configuration are not readable during the transition, called "the largest cost of the first months" (layer 1);
  - more prompts;
  - from phase 2 the sandbox breaks `git push`, `gh` and Docker;
  - 24/7 approver duty, with two people awake at night (§1);
  - up to 5 days to get a new tool approved.
- The brief and CLAUDE.md ask for every control's cost to engineers.
- *Fix:* add a one-line "What it costs engineers" row.

**M5. docs/02-engineer-guide.md:51 and diagrams/01-change-workflow.mmd:11 overstate who approves a normal PR.**
- Both say a normal domain PR is approved by "your domain team, or the on-call group".
- The OD9 process rule (framework 340-342) says otherwise: a group member approves another domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and they are on shift, and a monthly report counts the exceptions.
- *Fix:* add that limit in both places.

**M6. The guide has no section for engineers who are on the on-call approver rota.**
- What they need to know (framework Roles table line 102, §1 lines 71-73, layer 7):
  - 24/7 duty, with an approval wait of ≤ 15 min (S7);
  - while on call they only approve: no fix, no JIT request;
  - primary approves, backup only replaces an unavailable primary;
  - the cross-domain rule from M5;
  - a night incident needs two people awake.
- This is the largest new duty for engineers, and only the incident-responder side is described.
- *Fix:* add a short "When you are the on-call approver" section.

**M7. Guide §1 (lines 25-29) leaves out phase-2 changes engineers will notice, and one sentence is unconditional.**
- Missing:
  - `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`: an engineer's own and the project's allow rules are ignored, so prompts likely rise (framework 205);
  - sign-in is locked to Papaya's org, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `apiKeyHelper` sessions are refused (framework 209);
  - a minimum version floor;
  - a prompt for every WebFetch;
  - native Windows does not start, and on macOS localhost servers fail (examples/README 120-128).
- Line 28, "Each `aws`, `pulumi` or `serverless` call asks you first", only holds from phase 2 (the `ask` rules are in E8 phase 2). In phase 1 these calls run without a prompt in auto mode.
- *Fix:* add a short cost list and add "from phase 2, in auto mode too" to that sentence.

**M8. Guide §2, §4 and §5 leave out an action engineers must take.**
- Engineers must end the portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant (framework layer 2, lines 228-230). This protects the riskiest window against token theft.
- *Fix:* add it to the JIT and real-data steps.

**M9. Guide:13 and guide:95 make wrong statements about non-prod data.**
- "Non-prod is yours … no new approval" and "Non-prod holds no real data" are wrong during the transition. Stores not yet scanned follow the L3-data rule and are not part of the free loop (framework §1 line 46, layer 6 lines 579-581).
- "If you find some, report it" is a rule the framework does not contain.
- *Fix:* restate the unscanned-store rule and drop the new rule, or cite a source for it.

**M10. diagrams/02-identity-trust-boundaries.mmd:39-41 shows things the text doesn't say.**
- The `PROD → CT` edge says "every API call". The text says data events are on only for PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS, and that Aurora SQL is likely invisible (framework 608-617).
- `DEP -->|apply| DATA` suggests the deploy role writes claim data. It changes resources, not data.
- The GitHub audit-log export is drawn inside the log-archive account. Its destination is still open (register O-4), and the export starts in phase 2.
- *Fix:* relabel to "management events + selected data events", point the deploy edge at "prod resources", and mark the export destination as open.

### LOW
- **Guide:112:** CLAUDE.md changes are approved "by the L3 owner team, not only your domain team". It should say the L3 owner team *only*; a domain-team approval doesn't count (framework 297, 308-309).
- **Guide:57-58, risk-stop approval PR:**
  - By default the first approver approves it; another owner makes three people and is recorded as a deviation (OD13, OD11). The guide's "may be" understates this.
